name: truthstone-practices
description: Six skills that guide a coding agent to show evidence before saying a task is done: a requirement ledger, file:line grounding, scope checks, proportional planning, a pre-flight for irreversible shell commands, and a review of the diff against the request. Where the optional Truthstone checks tools are connected, three of the skills also ask them for a deterministic second opinion.

interface.longDescription:
Truthstone Practices adds six step-by-step protocols that a coding agent follows at specific points in a task: before reporting work as done, before relying on code it has not seen, before editing outside the request, when sizing a plan, before running an irreversible shell command, and before handing over a diff.

Skills included:
- Evidence Before Done: turns your request into a requirement ledger, including prohibitions such as "don't edit the tests", ties each item to evidence gathered after the last edit, and reports every item as verified, failed or not verified instead of a bare "done".
- Ground Claims: checks that a function, method, module, file, config key, route or package exists before code relies on it, cites file:line, says what does exist when something does not, and labels unverified assumptions.
- Scope Discipline: states the expected scope before editing, asks before out-of-scope changes, and follows the repository's existing conventions for file placement and naming.
- Proportional Planning: sizes the plan to the task. Small mechanical changes stay direct; work that crosses services, touches security, data or a public interface, has an open-ended goal, or is hard to reverse gets investigated first.
- Safe Shell: a pre-flight for deletions, history rewrites, destructive database statements, deployments and downloaded scripts that covers the exact target, whether it can be undone, a safer alternative, and your explicit go-ahead for anything irreversible.
- Diff Review: compares the complete diff with the request and looks for missing requirements, unrequested changes, stale references after renames, weakened or deleted tests, and unexplained dependencies or files.

How it works: the skills are instructions, and the plugin has no code and no hooks. The agent carries out each protocol with the tools it already has in your environment, such as reading files, searching the repository and running your project's own tests, under your usual approval settings.

Optional checks: the version in the ChatGPT and Codex plugin directory also connects Truthstone checks, a small hosted service with three read-only tools that apply Truthstone's deterministic rules to text the model passes in. check_shell_command reads a command line for destructive or irreversible effects; check_test_edit compares a test file before and after a change for skips, deleted tests and weaker assertions; check_test_runs reads the edits and commands of a task, in order, for a whole-suite test run that passed after the last edit, and for a final message that claims more than the runs show. The tools receive only that text, run nothing and store nothing. Without them, every skill works as written.

Who it is for: developers who use an agent to change code in a repository, for example in Codex. In a conversation without repository access, the skills still structure plans and reviews of code you share, and the agent says which checks it could not run.

Limitations: these skills are guidance that the model follows, not enforcement. They cannot block a command or a reply. Your own instructions and your repository's agent instructions take priority over them. Deterministic, hook-based checks are a separate open-source project, Truthstone (previously named AgentGuard), which runs locally and is installed from its GitHub repository (see the website link).
capabilities: Requirement ledger with verified, failed and not-verified items
file:line grounding for functions, files, config keys and packages
Scope statement and a check before out-of-scope edits
Plan depth sized to task complexity and risk
Diff review against the original request
Optional checks of shell commands, test file edits and test runs against Truthstone's rules
defaultPrompt: Finish this task, then show the evidence for each requirement before you call it done.
Before changing anything, size the plan for this task and tell me what is in scope.
Review my current diff against the task: stale references, weakened tests, out-of-scope edits.

publication.release_notes: 1.1.0: safe-shell, diff-review and evidence-before-done can ask the optional Truthstone checks tools (check_shell_command, check_test_edit, check_test_runs) for a deterministic second opinion, and fall back to their manual steps without them. The directory package declares the hosted Truthstone checks MCP server. 1.0.1: first release, six instruction-only skills.
